cards.q: What does the SD-WAN lab bring up and verify?
cards.a: It brings up the control plane (vManage/vSmart/vBond), onboards vEdge/cEdge routers, and verifies transport tunnels, BFD, and policy, modernizing WAN design with centralized control.

cards.q: What are the SD-WAN components and their roles?
cards.a: vManage is the dashboard, vSmart applies policy, vBond is the orchestrator, vEdge/cEdge are the routers, and vAnalytics handles reporting.

cards.q: What is the correct SD-WAN bring-up order?
cards.a: The control plane (vManage, vSmart, vBond) comes up first, then the data plane, so 'control plane first, data plane follows'.

cards.q: What is the vEdge/cEdge onboarding flow?
cards.a: Define the DNA/port, discover vBond, upload to vManage, contact vSmart, and then transport tunnels form.

cards.q: How does an edge router register in SD-WAN?
cards.a: The vEdge first finds vBond (the orchestrator), then registers to vManage and contacts vSmart.

cards.q: What commands verify SD-WAN control and tunnel health?
cards.a: show sdwan control connections, show sdwan control local-properties, show sdwan tunnel, show sdwan interface, and show sdwan policy.

cards.q: What is the first check when troubleshooting SD-WAN?
cards.a: show sdwan control connections, to confirm the control plane is up.

cards.q: How do BFD and SLA affect SD-WAN?
cards.a: BFD provides liveness, SLA provides class metrics, and together they drive path selection, path preference, and fallback with vSmart applying policy.

cards.q: What drives SD-WAN path selection and failover?
cards.a: BFD liveness and SLA metrics, which vSmart uses to apply policy for path preference and backup fallback.

cards.q: What are the SD-WAN policy types and their scope?
cards.a: Centralized policy is applied by vSmart, data policy uses match/action, control policy affects routing, localized policy applies at the device, and app-aware policy handles priority.
Policy is vSmart-applied match/action rules that govern data, control, and localized routing behavior.

cards.q: What is the SD-WAN lab flow?
cards.a: Deploy the controllers, onboard the edge, check control connections, bring up tunnels, apply policy, then verify.

cards.q: What is the default DTLS control-plane port used by SD-WAN?
cards.a: DTLS 12346 is used for the SD-WAN control plane.

cards.q: An edge router has no control connections. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A vBond discovery problem, so check show sdwan control connections.

cards.q: Transport tunnels are down in SD-WAN. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A TLOC issue, so check the tunnel state with show sdwan tunnel.

cards.q: SD-WAN policy is not being applied. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: vSmart is not pushing the policy, so check show sdwan policy.

cards.q: The SD-WAN data plane can be brought up before the control plane is ready.
cards.a: False — the control plane (vManage, vSmart, vBond) must be up first; the data plane follows.

cards.q: What port and protocol does the SD-WAN control plane use, and why does it matter?
cards.a: DTLS over UDP port 12346 carries control-plane signaling; knowing it helps verify and troubleshoot controller connectivity.
The control-connection and tunnel tables, verified with show sdwan control connections and show sdwan tunnel.
